scope: Complete distribution tooling and beta1 manifest; thirteen unchanged application runtime files were assessed in the earlier full review.

findings.title: Manifest <files>/<languages> entries are never cross-checked against the packaged file allowlist
findings.fact: bgm_manifest_details() in bgm-scripts/bgm-build.py only inspects the FIRST <files><folder> element via manifest.find('files/folder') (the 'services' folder). It never inspects the other two <folder> entries (src, bgm-assets), the three <filename> entries (bgm-bootstrap.php, bgm-styler.php, bgm-licence.txt), or the <languages> block. BGM_ALLOWED_FILES in the same script is a separately hand-maintained Python set that is only compared against the on-disk/zip file list, never against what the XML manifest itself declares for installation. A future manifest edit that drops a <filename>/<folder>/<language> entry (so Joomla would silently skip installing that file) would still pass bgm_build() and bgm_package_receipt() unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Derive the expected file set by parsing the manifest's <files>/<languages> elements (expanding <folder> entries recursively) and compare it against BGM_ALLOWED_FILES, so a build fails the moment the manifest's declared install paths and the shipped files diverge.

findings.title: Generated update-feed candidate XML is written with owner-only (0600) permissions
findings.fact: bgm-scripts/bgm-feed.py's bgm_generate() writes output via tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=output_path.parent, ...) then Path.replace(). CPython's NamedTemporaryFile hardcodes file mode 0600 on POSIX (tempfile._mkstemp_inner), unaffected by umask since 0600 has no group/other bits, and rename()/replace() preserves the source inode's permission bits rather than the destination's. The resulting bgm-update-<version>.xml therefore ends up owner-read/write-only, unlike the archive/receipt files bgm-build.py writes via Path.write_bytes()/write_text(), which get normal umask-based permissions.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly os.chmod(temporary_path, 0o644) before the atomic replace() so the published artifact is world-readable regardless of which user runs the build versus the publish/web-serving process.

findings.title: targetplatform version constraint is anchored at only one end
findings.fact: bgm-scripts/bgm-feed.py's bgm_feed_xml() emits <targetplatform name="joomla" version="6\.2\.0$"/> — the fragment has a trailing $ but no leading ^. Depending on exactly how Joomla's updater wraps this fragment in its own preg_match against JVERSION, an unanchored start would let the constraint match any version string ending in '6.2.0' (e.g. a hypothetical future '16.2.0'), not only '6.2.0' itself.
findings.recommendation: Anchor both ends explicitly (^6\.2\.0$) so the platform qualification doesn't rely on an assumption about how the installer wraps the supplied pattern.

findings.title: ZIP member timestamps use a literal hardcoded calendar date instead of a documented constant
findings.fact: bgm_build() in bgm-scripts/bgm-build.py stamps every ZipInfo with the literal tuple (2026, 10, 18, 0, 0, 0) — today's date at authoring time — rather than a fixed epoch (e.g. the zip default 1980-01-01) or a value derived from the release itself. Every future rebuild of any future version will keep embedding '2026-10-18' as the per-file timestamp, which is reproducible but factually incorrect metadata for later releases.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit epoch constant, or derive the stamp from the manifest's <creationDate> or another release-specific input, instead of a literal date that will go stale.

findings.title: Frozen 0.1.0 compatibility special-case is permanently embedded in the forward build path
findings.fact: bgm_manifest_details() in bgm-scripts/bgm-build.py special-cases version == '0.1.0' to forbid an <updateservers> block, solely to keep validating the already-frozen, previously-shipped 0.1.0 prototype referenced in REVIEW-SCOPE.txt. This historical-only branch runs inside the same validator every future 0.1.x/1.x build will execute.
findings.recommendation: Move the one-off validation of the frozen 0.1.0 artifact into a separate historical-compatibility check/test outside the primary build path, so the production validator only encodes rules for versions that can still be built going forward.

adjudicationStatus: Narrow repairs passed independent adversarial review and authoritative correction review. No remaining demonstrated release-tooling blocker.

adjudication.basis: Exact native files/languages declarations and complete allowlist coverage are required for build and ZIP receipt. Eight missing declarations plus altered ZIP regression pass.

adjudication.decision: Repaired local public-artifact mode; GitHub access already passed
adjudication.basis: Mode0644 applied before atomic replace and verified by actual stat. GitHub raw output does not inherit POSIX0600 and was anonymously200 before repair.
Both native XML adapters prepend a start anchor; native discovery confirms the exact qualified version selection. XML fragment retained.
Named documented constant retains identical ZIP bytes; timestamp is not a claim about future file creation dates.
Frozen0.1.0 receipt can be validated without retroactive feed registration. Feed generator still rejects its no-feed installer.
